items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Well, most of the greats they had -- Roland James of Sonny and Sonny...

ctx.x: Well, most of the greats they had -- Roland James of Sonny and Sonny, Sonny Austin of the Four (Unintelligible) and Baby Lawrence of the Harlem Highlanders. Well, then, Groundhog -- he was coming out of retirement at another time -- at that time. Because he had been a popular dancer with the Whitman sisters. And then you had Taps Miller -- that was the tap dancing trumpet player. He composed songs like, 'Wham, rebop, boom, bam, I'm killer-diller, yes I am. Wham, bebop, boom, bam, I can sing and I can jam.' And he…
Let me ask you, did novelty tap start prior to this particular era, which is the big band era? Were there novelty acts?
